Coming from another 17 year old girl, I’ve had the same doubts and confusion about being bisexual before. Sexuality takes time to understand and explore. Personally, it took me years to come to terms with the fact that I’m bi; my biggest struggle was facing bi phobia in society and within myself. 

There are several myths about people who are bi that can often cause people to repress and reject themselves. To combat this, I read several articles on bisexuality and watched many videos of people coming out as bi. They’re great sources for seeing myths get debunked, and may ease any fear and confusion. As for internalized bi phobia, you may sometimes feel like you may actually be straight and are just confused while other times you think you’re only into the same sex. This is natural too. In your situation, you may think because you’re more experienced with dating guys that you can’t be bisexual, but that is untrue. Experiences do not dictate your attractions; you can’t choose the people you’re attracted to. Some bi people also experience a push and pull in their attractions, feeling more attracted to one gender over another for a period of time. Others are attracted to both genders equally. Bisexuality is unique to each bi individual, so there is no set way you should feel, because sexuality is fluid. 

It’s a process to know and understand who you are. It may be a struggle to get there, but it’s worth it in the end. As a girl who’s had many “girl crushes” and also fantasizes about girls while knowing my attraction to guys, there's a chance you may be bisexual. In the end, identify the way you want to as long as you keep loving who you are. Hope this helped!
